column1: # Readings of a customs heading that hold only for part of its rows (series, period, unit), applied by human_trade/scripts/build_skos_v4.py.
# The heading keeps its id and general anchor; each row here becomes its own oe:ScopedReading node with the count of Layer-1 rows inside its scope.
# series_regex / unit_regex are case-insensitive regular expressions on the printed (or inferred) series and the printed unit; blank = any. status: supported | probable | unresolved.

column11: Annual Statements 1856–66 enter the article by number, from the British West India Islands and British Guiana; cacao was entered by weight under 'Cocoa'.
CUST 4 and CUST 5 ledgers 1800–1840 enter these rows by weight; early ledgers used 'cocoa nuts' for cacao as well as for coconuts, and nothing in the rows settles which.
The single 1840 CUST 4 row is entered by number, the form later used for coconuts; one row is thin evidence.
